result_text:
**The data doesn't support the claim, but it can't fully rule it out.** The file covers only the first 20 hours of 2026-07-15, and the claim is about the whole day.

- **p95 is about 392 ms.** That comes from the 1,200 requests in the file, and the 95% interval is roughly 378–410 ms. I computed it as a rank interval with a normal approximation. 500 ms lies well outside it.
- **No single hour reached 500 ms.** The highest hourly p95 was 460 ms, at 15:00. Only 14 of the 1,200 requests (about 1.2%) took longer than 500 ms, and the slowest was 709 ms. A few individual slow requests may be what the person saw.
- **The last four hours are missing.** The file has one row per minute from 00:00Z to 19:59Z and nothing from 20:00Z to 23:59Z. I can't tell whether those requests didn't happen, weren't logged, or weren't exported. A bad evening could in principle push the full-day p95 above 500 ms, though it would have to be a very bad four hours. Hours 15 and 19 were the two highest, at 460 ms and 437 ms, which is a mild reason to look at that gap rather than a trend.
- **The timezone of "yesterday" is unstated.** I assumed UTC.

To close this out, pull the 20:00–23:59 data or tell me the timezone the claim uses. I'd also ask the person where their number came from, since a dashboard may be using a different window or percentile method.

I treated this as a single claim to check, so I didn't test competing explanations. The ledger is at `/var/folders/4_/s6fbcjyn4b13xdxkd3lv0kw00000gn/T/arm-s11-post-2-bxuuwsu4/work/ledger.md`.
